<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Previously, we would only set the `Time` property, which `EndTime` would set for us. However, we had no frame of reference as to when the data was began being aggregated. 

In addition to this, we had no mechanism to model the delay from the API when retrieving data from it. I have set this delay to zero for the meanwhile.

pr_comments:
- Lean is using `EndTime` so there shouldn't be an issue since the end times are always going forward
- Since the offset is less than the data resolution ( Minute right? ) it might be rounded down, see https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Engine/DataFeeds/SubscriptionData.cs#L65 where we will round down before emitting - I think this could potentially happen in other places too.
 - The overlapping could confuse users.

Could we use a 1 minute offset instead? Would be pessimistic but would avoid these issues

> 
> 
>     * Lean is using `EndTime` so there shouldn't be an issue since the end times are always going forward
> 
>     * Since the offset is less than the data resolution ( Minute right? ) it might be rounded down, see https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Engine/DataFeeds/SubscriptionData.cs#L65 where we will round down before emitting - I think this could potentially happen in other places too.
> 
>     * The overlapping could confuse users.
> 
> 
> Could we use a 1 minute offset instead? Would be pessimistic but would avoid these issues

Solely based on the fact that we will have time rounded down on us is enough to set a 1 minute offset. However, we should try to also aim to model live trading as accurately as possible. I'd like to discuss a solution with you if possible since there's a lot to consider here 👍

- @gsalaz98 reviewed the stack and it seems that the only sticky point would be consolidators not being triggered https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Engine/AlgorithmManager.cs#L1277 which do not exist today.
- My round down comment isn't valid because its applied on the data.Time and the offset is in the data.EndTime - see https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Engine/DataFeeds/SubscriptionData.cs#L65 closely
- Regarding history requests specifying bar counts as periods https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Algorithm/QCAlgorithm.History.cs#L199, since the underlying implementation uses resolution it might cause it to not include some data point, since end time might be after, but note that PsychSignalSentiment is flagged as sparse data too, so the behavior of this api call wouldn't be that deterministic either way

Any feedback on the Travis errors?

```Errors and Failures:
1) Test Failure : QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes(AAPL.TiingoNews R735QTJ8XC9W,Hour,1,0,0,0,0,48,False)
     Expected: 48
  But was:  47

at QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes (QuantConnect.Symbol symbol, QuantConnect.Resolution resolution, System.Int32 days, System.Int32 expectedTicksReceived, System.Int32 expectedTradeBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedQuoteBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedAuxPointsReceived, System.Int32 expectedCustomPointsReceived, System.Boolean shouldThrowException) [0x00ab0] in <81539c702ded4bbc88110d66c72d5b06>:0

2) Test Failure : QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes(AAPL.TiingoNews R735QTJ8XC9W,Minute,1,0,0,0,0,120,False)
     Expected: 120
  But was:  119

at QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes (QuantConnect.Symbol symbol, QuantConnect.Resolution resolution, System.Int32 days, System.Int32 expectedTicksReceived, System.Int32 expectedTradeBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedQuoteBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedAuxPointsReceived, System.Int32 expectedCustomPointsReceived, System.Boolean shouldThrowException) [0x00ab0] in <81539c702ded4bbc88110d66c72d5b06>:0

3) Test Failure : QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes(AAPL.TiingoNews R735QTJ8XC9W,Tick,1,0,0,0,0,24,False)
     Expected: 24
  But was:  23

at QuantConnect.Tests.Engine.DataFeeds.LiveTradingDataFeedTests.HandlesAllTypes (QuantConnect.Symbol symbol, QuantConnect.Resolution resolution, System.Int32 days, System.Int32 expectedTicksReceived, System.Int32 expectedTradeBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedQuoteBarsReceived, System.Int32 expectedAuxPointsReceived, System.Int32 expectedCustomPointsReceived, System.Boolean shouldThrowException) [0x00ab0] in <81539c702ded4bbc88110d66c72d5b06>:0
```

After some thought and inspection, I'm pretty sure that the test is failing because of my changes 😢 

Probably with the time advances, we can't squeeze in an additional data point per day, causing the number of points to drop from 24 to 23, 48 to 47, and 120 to 119. 

This is backed up by the fact that the `FuncDataQueueHandler` uses `PsychSignalSentiment` as the custom data to emit, and sets the `EndTime` parameter, causing it to be advanced 15s into the future:

https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/cf1b6c340aae834058827db4c3c9a6cbbf98ad9b/Tests/Engine/DataFeeds/LiveTradingDataFeedTests.cs#L1319-L1345

@StefanoRaggi - Could you please review the test to see if my changes are the source of the test failing?

review_comments: @jaredbroad  -- I still think we should have done `BaseData.Period` :P
A note for posterity... in LEAN, the `EndTime` is the *only* time that matters. We don't (or at least _shouldn't_) use the `Time` property for anything in the engine.
